keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Cleves row). The page names the towns Cleves, Wesel, Xanten, Emmerich, Rees and Duisburg and gives no area; a 28 km circle at Cleves (about 2,500 km2) is a stand-in, soft. Count Johann died in 1368 and his nephew Adolph III of the Marck inherited.

correction.text: with the County of Mark (Hamm and the Mark Oberhof), united 1391 / 1394

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: infobox 'United with Mark: 1391'; the Mark page: 'In 1391, Adolph III also inherited the Mark from his elder brother Engelbert III' and 'united both counties as Cleves-Mark in 1394'. The county 'enclosed an area of approximately 3,000 km2'; a 31 km circle at 7.55E 51.52N is 3,000 km2. Cleves was raised to a duchy in 1417 and from 1521 was in personal union with Jülich-Berg (the United Duchies). Revised after review: ends 1448 because Soest joins in 1449 (next keyframe).

correction.text: Cleves-Mark with Soest, which 'remained part of the Duchy of Cleves' after the Soest Feud, with Soest

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Duchy of Westphalia page: 'The town of Soest was lost to the Duchy of Cleves-Mark after the Soest Feud in 1449' and 'After the Soest Feud, the city of Soest remained part of the Duchy of Cleves'. The 15 km circle at 8.11E 51.57N is the stand-in for the town and its Börde and lies about 40 km east of the Mark circle. The pre-review shape left Soest undrawn 1449-1614. Revised after review: Soest circle added (gained 1449).

The Cleves page has the United Provinces occupying 'large parts of the Duchy of Cleves' until the Franco-Dutch War in 1672, which belongs to the Brandenburg dossier. ledger.note: 1092: the first documented lord. 'The first documented lord from the House of Cleves is Dietrich, numbered variously as II or III, in 1092' (the page also dates the ancestor Rutger von Antoing's enfeoffment of imperial property near Kleve to 1020).

region.text: the County of Cleves round Cleves on the lower Rhine

ledger.note: 1368: the La Marck dynasty. After Count Johann died in 1368 'the fief was inherited by his nephew Adolf III of the Marck'; Mark page: Adolph III 'acquired the County of Cleves on the western banks of the Rhine in 1368'. Same state, new dynasty.

1391: Mark. 'In 1391, Adolph III also inherited the Mark from his elder brother Engelbert III' (infobox 'United with Mark: 1391'); the Mark page says he 'united both counties as Cleves-Mark in 1394'. The Cleves page puts the personal union after Engelbert III died without issue in 1391.

region.text: the County of Mark round Hamm, about 3,000 km2

ledger.note: 1417: King Sigismund 'raised Count Adolph I to the status of a duke and a Prince of the Holy Roman Empire in 1417', and the county became a duchy.

5 June 1444: Soest rejects Archbishop Dietrich of Cologne by 'accepting a new suzerain, John I of Cleves-Mark, the Duke of Cleves-Mark', who guaranteed the town its old rights; the feud runs 'from 1444 to 1449'. Mirror of the contest events in electorate-of-cologne.

region.text: the town of Soest and its Börde

ledger.note: 1449: the Soest Feud ends; the page's bibliography dates its end to 27 April of the year (the anniversary 'Beendigung der Soester Fehde am 27. April 1949'), so April 1449 is implied, not stated; the month is left out. The page names no treaty.

1449: Soest passes to Cleves-Mark. 'The town of Soest was lost to the Duchy of Cleves-Mark after the Soest Feud in 1449'; 'After the Soest Feud, the city of Soest remained part of the Duchy of Cleves'. Mirror of the Cologne loss. The Soest Feud page says only that the town took John I of Cleves-Mark as suzerain; Soest was an enclave in Cologne's land, so the 15 km circle is a stand-in for the town and its Börde.

region.text: the town of Soest and its Börde

ledger.note: 10 June 1609: the Treaty of Dortmund. After Duke John William of Jülich-Cleves-Berg died on 25 March 1609 without heirs, Brandenburg and Neuburg set up a provisional joint government as the 'possessors'.

region.text: the Duchy of Cleves and the County of Mark

ledger.note: 12 November 1614: 'Eventually, the Treaty of Xanten was approved on 12 November 1614.' The Dutch had 'occupied Mark and Cleves' and the Spanish took Wesel earlier in 1614 (no dates on the page).

12 November 1614: Cleves-Mark goes to Brandenburg. 'Cleves-Mark and Ravensberg went to George William of Brandenburg' (War of the Jülich Succession page); infobox 'To Brandenburg: 1614'; Cleves was 'finally incorporated into Brandenburg-Prussia' in 1666.

region.text: the Duchy of Cleves and the County of Mark and Soest

wars.name: Soest Feud
wars.outcome: Soest, an enclave in Cologne's land, takes John I of Cleves-Mark as suzerain on 5 June 1444 and stays with the Duchy of Cleves after the feud ends in 1449 (the Feud page gives no treaty; its bibliography implies 27 April 1449).

wars.name: War of the Jülich Succession (Cleves-Mark)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Xanten (12 November 1614) gave Cleves-Mark and Ravensberg to Brandenburg; the Dutch held Cleves and Mark and the Spanish took Wesel in 1614.

certainty.note: The pages give towns and dukes, not boundaries; the only area is 'approximately 3,000 km2' for the Mark.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (3 pages; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no Cleves row.

SCOPE. The state is Cleves with Mark from 1391, ending when the electorate of Brandenburg takes both at Xanten in 1614 (infobox). The Cleves page has the final incorporation into Brandenburg-Prussia in 1666 and French annexation of the left bank in 1795 (Peace of Basel); those are Brandenburg-Prussia's events. The county of Mark before 1391 (Berg-Altena 1160; the page puts the seat at Altena, then Burg Mark near Hamm in the 1220s; Hamm founded 1226) is county-of-mark, not drawn here.

SHAPES are circles (gazetteer lacks the towns): Cleves 6.40E 51.72N 28 km; Mark 7.55E 51.52N 31 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Cleves' (Kleve), 'Wesel', 'Hamm'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The union with Mark: 1391 on the infobox and Cleves text, 1394 on the Mark page. (2) The extent of Cleves before 1391 and the towns it held (Duisburg, Rees, Xanten, Emmerich only as 'towns' on the page). (3) The 1614 Dutch and Spanish occupations are undated on the page; the Dutch held 'large parts of the Duchy of Cleves' until 1672. (4) The Cleves page does not mention a 1666 treaty (the War of the Jülich Succession page has the Treaty of Cleves 1666). (5) The Soest Feud (1444-1449) and the loss of Soest are not on any page opened: the Mark page 'does not mention' it; electorate-of-cologne has Soest. (6) The United Duchies (1521) are a personal union and not drawn.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: county-of-mark (to 1391), palatinate-neuburg, julich-cleves-berg (umbrella).

REVISION 2026-10-25 (after review). Soest added: contest 1444 (5 June, Soest Feud page) to 1449 against electorate-of-cologne and a 1449 gain (Duchy of Westphalia page: 'lost to the Duchy of Cleves-Mark after the Soest Feud in 1449'), mirroring the Cologne dossier's contest events and loss; K1 split at 1449, the Soest circle (8.11E 51.57N, 15 km) is in K1b, K2, the dissolve and the Brandenburg successor land; the Soest Feud is in wars. The Feud page does not say Soest became part of the Duchy (it names only John I as 'new suzerain'); the Westphalia page does ('remained part of the Duchy of Cleves'), and that page is the one used. The Feud page's end is implied by its bibliography ('Beendigung der Soester Fehde am 27. April 1949'), so no month is entered.
